blocks.text: The best way to understand how to interpret an IR spectrum is by looking at solved examples and becoming familiar with the characteristic features of an IR spectrum.

blocks.title: Example 29.1
blocks.problem: Examine the two spectra shown and determine which one belongs to propan-2-ol and which one belongs to propanone.
steps: The presence of a strong, sharp absorption around 1710 cm corresponds to the characteristic C=O, carbonyl, the functional group in a ketone. IR spectrum A is propanone.
In spectrum B the presence of a strong, absorption around 3200−3600 cm suggests that there is an alcohol group present, which corresponds to the -OH group in propan-2-ol.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The unit of wavenumber is printed as “cm”; it is cm⁻¹: 1710 cm⁻¹ and 3200−3600 cm⁻¹.

blocks.alt: Two infrared spectra, A (top) and B (bottom), each plotted as absorbance / % (0 at the top, 100 at the bottom) against wavenumber/cm^-1 from 4000 to 500. A has a small dip near 3450, a strong band near 3000 and a very strong, sharp band near 1750, then several bands below 1500. B has a very broad, deep band centred near 3350, strong bands near 2950 and many bands below 1500.
